image_description: An underwater photograph of a hammerhead shark swimming diagonally from the bottom-left to the top-right. The distinctive T-shaped cephalofoil (hammer head) is clearly visible on the left, with eyes at the tips. The body is streamlined and greyish-green, fading into the blue water background. The first dorsal fin and pectoral fins are visible.

The skin appears overly smooth and plastic-like due to the combination of water diffusion and low resolution, lacking the expected granular texture of shark skin, though this is likely photographic rather than generative.
